scope: B2wPiper, OFFICIAL ATEC-TaskB-B2wPiper env, single env, camera-free. One run, seed 42, `--mode stance_descend`.
question: How far below its settled height can this chassis carry its body, wheels planted, before the official illegal_contact fires?
interpretation: The chassis carried a full 0.253 m of vertical body travel with every wheel still on the ground and ZERO force on all nine official contact bodies. The earlier belief that a deep crouch necessarily trips illegal_contact came from a full-amplitude open-loop crouch probe (left-rear thigh, 1082 N at body z 0.326); this run shows the reachable envelope is much larger when the descent is solved geometrically instead of driven open-loop. Only 0.10 m of the 0.255 m drift happens while the body is moving; the rest accumulates once it has already stopped at the bottom, so a descent that must hold an aim needs a wheel-angle brake, not just a zero wheel velocity.

settled_object_heights.note: Measured from the same run's telemetry, not derived. All six objects of each type settle to the same height within 2e-6 m.

ground_height_correction.finding: The Task B ground surface is at world z = +0.0449, not 0.
ground_height_correction.basis: task_b/terrain.py builds the ground as a box of height 0.10 translated to z = -0.005, so its top face is at +0.045; independently, all 18 settled object roots sit 0.0408-0.0446 m above the height their resting geometry predicts for a z=0 ground.
ground_height_correction.consequence: Every earlier object-top figure in this project that assumed the ground at z=0 is 4.5 cm too low. With the corrected tops the Piper's fingertips reach 1.5 cm BELOW the tallest object from the unmodified natural stance, not 3 cm above it -- see piper_gripper_and_reach.json for the reach limit itself, which is unaffected.

grasp_envelope_by_object_type.note: required_body_z = object top - 0.03 m clearance + 0.2937 m of fingertip reach below the body origin. All three types are reachable inside the measured envelope.

not_shown: One seed, one run. This measures the stance only: no grasp, no delivery, no score, and no claim that the body can hold any of these depths under a load or while a task is performed.
